title: Jensen Huang resigns: how the Nvidia espionage reports unfolded
dek: In two weeks, a report that Nvidia’s founder was targeted by Chinese intelligence led to a board inquiry, a second allegation, a share slide and his resignation.
seoTitle: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO: full timeline of the espionage scandal
bigLabel: Nvidia was once worth about $5 trillion, per Yahoo Finance

glance.what: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on 12 November, two weeks after The New York Times reported that US intelligence found he had a close relationship with a Megaspeed executive they concluded was working for Beijing. Huang admitted infidelity, the board hired outside investigators, and a second alleged relationship, with a senior Nvidia executive, was reported on 11 November.
glance.why: Nvidia makes the chips behind most of the world’s AI and is one of the most valuable companies on earth. Its founder leaving under investigation raises questions about US–China chip security, who runs the company next, and what it means for investors.
glance.next: Interim CEO Colette Kress leads Nvidia’s earnings on 17 November. House committees still want to hear from Huang, and the board is searching for a permanent CEO.

forYou: If you hold Nvidia shares or tech funds, expect volatility around the 17 November earnings and the CEO search. No outlet has reported that Huang broke any law or that Nvidia secrets were lost; the espionage claims are allegations that China denies, and the second relationship is reported, not confirmed.

events.title: New York Times report: Huang targeted by Chinese intelligence
events.summary: US intelligence agencies found Huang had developed a close relationship with an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, one of Nvidia’s biggest Southeast Asian customers, whom US officials concluded was gathering information for Beijing. Officials did not believe Huang knew. Nvidia said the interactions were a normal part of his job. China called the claims baseless smears.

events.title: House committee chairs ask Huang for a closed-door briefing
events.summary: Three Republican House committee chairs ask Huang to brief them on 18 November about his contacts with the Megaspeed executive and Nvidia’s protections against espionage, with a reply due by 11 November. The letter comes a day after midterms in which Republicans lost control of Congress.

events.title: Incoming Democratic majority signals its own questions
events.summary: Bloomberg reports that the new Democratic majority in Congress is set to demand answers from Nvidia on keeping its AI chips out of China. The new Congress sits from 3 January.

events.title: Board opens independent investigation; Huang admits infidelity
events.summary: A committee of independent directors with outside counsel will review the reports. The board says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised and that it has confidence in Huang, who stays CEO. In a message to staff, Huang says he was unfaithful to his wife and will cooperate fully. President Trump calls him an honourable man and says he has not discussed the matter with him.

events.title: Shares slide; China rejects the claims
events.summary: Nvidia falls as much as 8% in early trading before recovering to about 4% down, while rivals AMD and Broadcom rise. China’s Foreign Ministry calls the allegations unsubstantiated. Huang pulls out of an AI industry CEO forum.

events.title: Former US attorney and Wachtell Lipton hired to run the inquiry
events.summary: The board names Joon Kim, a former acting US Attorney, and the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead the independent investigation. Nvidia’s losses since Monday reach close to $500 billion in market value, according to NBC News.
events.differs: NBC News puts the fall at more than 10% since Monday; CNN reported the shares down over 5% for the week on 11 November.

events.title: New report alleges a second relationship, with a senior Nvidia executive
events.summary: The New York Times reports, citing five employees, that Huang is also suspected of a relationship with a married executive who reports directly to him. Nvidia has rules discouraging relationships between managers and subordinates. This is a reported allegation; Nvidia’s response had not been published in the coverage we reviewed. Analysts have started asking whether Huang could be forced to step aside, with no public succession plan.

events.title: Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO
events.summary: After a board meeting on Wednesday night, Nvidia says its co-founder has stepped down as chief executive. Chief financial officer Colette Kress takes over on an interim basis, and venture investor Harvey C. Jones becomes the company’s first board chair. The board is reported to be looking at outside candidates for the permanent role. Investigations by the FBI and Congress, and a shareholder class-action lawsuit, continue.
events.differs: Yahoo Finance reports the shares fell as much as 13% before recovering; StockTitan had them down 4.5% by early afternoon New York time.
